variants.label: Leads · SMB
variants.reader_job: Plan a secondhand equipment purchase for a small business while keeping a personal budget clear.
variants.subject: A used camera hunt can start with one message
variants.preheader: Meet Tix, a conversational approach to secondhand buying. Start with the item you need and the amount you can spend.

paragraphs.text: Your next product shoot needs a camera. You have a budget in mind, and a few minutes between everything else that needs doing.
We're building Tix to start that secondhand hunt with a conversation. Tell it what you're looking for and where to look. Add the most you're willing to spend.

For example: “I'm in Brooklyn, looking for a used Sony camera for less than $950.” That gives the conversation a useful starting point. In the preview, Tix compares an item's asking price with the limit you've chosen.
paragraphs.basis: Approved illustrative buyer brief, not an offer or a result

paragraphs.text: The walkthrough shows how the conversation is designed to work. Live marketplace sources are part of the next stage. Join the waitlist to follow what we're building.

variants.label: Leads · Agency
variants.reader_job: Turn a shoot's equipment need into a clear buying brief without inventing agency collaboration features.
variants.subject: Give your next camera hunt a clearer brief
variants.preheader: A client shoot starts with a brief. Tix brings that same clarity to the secondhand equipment you're looking for.

paragraphs.text: A client shoot can leave you with one small job that takes longer than expected: finding a used camera within the production budget.
Tix is being built around a buying conversation. Start with the equipment you want, then explain your location and spending limit in your own words.

The launch walkthrough follows someone looking for a used Sony in Brooklyn for less than $950. It's a specific brief you could adapt to your next shoot. The preview's price comparison uses the buyer's own limit.
paragraphs.basis: Approved creative scenario, not a customer testimonial

paragraphs.text: Supported marketplace sources and chosen notification channels are on the roadmap. If secondhand equipment is part of how you plan a shoot, join the waitlist and follow the next stage of Tix.

variants.label: Leads · Reseller / Affiliate
variants.reader_job: Evaluate and explain the buying workflow without invented resale margins, commissions or partner entitlements.
variants.subject: Before the next secondhand buy, set your limit
variants.preheader: See how Tix starts with a buyer's brief, and what its preview can tell you about a price before you go further.

paragraphs.text: When you're sizing up a secondhand item, the asking price is only part of the decision. You also need to know the most you're willing to pay.
paragraphs.basis: General reader guidance; no resale outcome claimed

paragraphs.text: Tix starts with that context. The product is being built for secondhand buyers and sellers, with a conversation about an item or listing. In the preview, a price comparison uses the buyer's chosen limit. Market value still needs its own evidence.
The camera walkthrough gives you a concrete way to understand the idea: a buyer in Brooklyn wants a used Sony for less than $950. It follows the intended experience from that first request.
If you evaluate secondhand gear or share useful buying tools with your audience, join the waitlist to follow Tix as it develops.
paragraphs.basis: Conditional audience relevance; no affiliate program or payout implied

variants.label: Customers · SMB
variants.reader_job: Give a returning preview reader a practical way to prepare the next equipment request.
variants.subject: Start your next Tix brief with a firm budget
variants.preheader: A useful way to explore the preview: choose one item for your business, then give Tix the buying limit you have in mind.

paragraphs.text: Before you buy the next piece of equipment for your business, write down the most you'd be comfortable spending. That number belongs in the first message.
paragraphs.basis: Editorial exercise for a returning preview reader

paragraphs.text: Tix's preview is designed around a conversation about what you're looking for. You can describe the item and your location, then set a limit. The price comparison uses that limit when you review an asking price.
The camera walkthrough starts with a used Sony in Brooklyn for less than $950. Think about the equivalent request for your business. A clear brief gives you a specific buying decision to explore.
paragraphs.basis: Approved scenario followed by a suggested reader exercise

paragraphs.text: The preview demonstrates the flow with stored examples. Live sources are planned for the next stage. Join the waitlist if you'd like to follow that progress.

variants.label: Customers · Agency
variants.reader_job: Help a returning agency reader prepare a shoot-specific purchasing exercise for the preview.
variants.subject: Use your next shoot to shape a Tix brief
variants.preheader: Use a real shoot to frame your next preview: decide which camera you need and what you'd be willing to pay for it.

paragraphs.text: Pick an upcoming shoot and the piece of equipment you'd consider buying used. Set aside a moment to agree on the spending limit before anyone starts looking.
paragraphs.basis: Suggested agency exercise; no built-in team approval feature implied

paragraphs.text: That brief fits the way Tix is being designed. The conversation starts with an item and a location. From there, a buyer can explain the price limit they have in mind.
In the preview, Tix compares the asking price with that limit. Use the walkthrough to see how the brief becomes a buying conversation, then consider which details your team would want to bring to it.
paragraphs.basis: Suggested review of the walkthrough; no live preview access promised

paragraphs.text: The roadmap includes supported marketplace sources and notifications through channels the user chooses. Join the waitlist to follow those next steps as Tix develops.
